title: Lost ₹45,000 to a Fake OLX Buyer Asking to 'Scan QR Code to Receive Money'
author: Rajesh M. (Pune)
description: I listed a sofa set on OLX. A buyer claiming to be a military officer contacted me and said he wanted to pay immediately via UPI. He sent me a QR code on WhatsApp saying 'Scan this QR code to receive ₹15,000 advance'. I didn't know QR codes are ONLY used to PAY money, not receive! I scanned it and entered my UPI PIN, and instantly ₹15,000 was deducted. Before I realized, he tricked me into scanning twice more to 'refund' the money.
lesson: NEVER enter your UPI PIN to receive money! Entering a PIN ALWAYS deducts money from your account.

title: ATM Card Skimmer at a Remote Highway ATM Machine
author: Anonymous
description: While driving on a highway, I stopped at an unattended non-bank ATM. The card slot felt a bit loose, but I ignored it. Two days later, I received 4 consecutive SMS alerts for cash withdrawals totaling ₹20,000 in another city! Cyber cell told me a fake card reader (skimmer) and hidden camera had cloned my magnetic stripe and stolen my PIN while I typed it uncovered.
lesson: Always check if the ATM slot is firm, cover the keypad with your hand when typing PIN, and prefer ATMs inside bank branches with guards.

title: Fake Electricity Bill Disconnection SMS & AnyDesk Remote Access Scam
author: Sunita K. (Mumbai)
description: I received an urgent SMS: 'Dear consumer your power will be disconnected at 9:30 PM due to unpaid bill of ₹12. Call 98xx-xxx-xxx'. Flustered, I called. The fake officer asked me to install an app called 'AnyDesk' for quick live verification. Once installed, he asked me to pay ₹10 via my netbanking app. Because he had live view of my screen, he captured my netbanking password & OTP and cleared ₹1.2 Lakhs!
lesson: Never download screen sharing apps (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk) at the request of strangers or alleged official caller!

title: Search Engine Fake Customer Care Number Scam for Bank Refund
author: Ankit S. (Bengaluru)
description: My transaction failed on a shopping site but money was deducted. I searched Google for 'XYZ Bank Toll Free Helpline'. The top search result (which was a paid ad) had a bogus number. I called it, and the fraudster posed as a bank manager. He persuaded me to share an OTP received on my phone claiming it was a 'Refund Verification Code'.
lesson: Never trust bank contact numbers found on Google search results or social media. Always use official numbers printed behind your debit card or official bank website.
